report:
Reviewed the full fresh crates.sage_ir.types.body.coroutines claim, its sole implementation association, and complete associated test. The requirements are: an async block has a typed nested coroutine body; an async function has a typed nested coroutine body; and Typed IR retains that high-level form rather than lowering it into a generator state machine. Both source forms and the negative lowering constraint must be established for a complete implementation verdict.

The only implementation association is the explicit sage_meta::todo entry in crates/sage-meta/tests/representation_spec.rs, stating that async/coroutine body representation remains pending. The only annotated test, sage_meta::todo::types_body_coroutines, has exactly that explanatory TODO and no assertions. There are no ordinary implementation or test associations and no N/A entries. Passing the placeholder cannot demonstrate typed nested bodies, either source form, or the absence of generator lowering in successfully represented coroutine output.

Captured the current TyBodyData, TyExpr, and full TyExprData enum as a representation dependency. The body has a root, locals and span; expressions carry type and span. The enum includes Await and Closure forms but no dedicated async/coroutine body form. General typed-expression structure and an await expression are insufficient evidence of the claimed nested coroutine representation. This supports the explicit pending representation prerequisite, without claiming that a missing variant alone proves the behavior of every parser/checker path. No production completeness verdict is made from these partial representation facilities.

Captured the typed-IR destination table and accepted architectural-foundations completed-tree rationale. The table includes both async blocks and async function bodies; the rationale explicitly keeps async bodies above MIR and excludes coroutine state-machine layout. These explain the intended representation boundary but are not executable evidence. The absence of generator machinery in an unfinished representation does not independently satisfy the complete claim.

The existing deferral honestly accounts for all requirements. Replacing it requires coroutine representation and checking for both async blocks and async functions, plus annotated tests directly inspecting typed nested bodies and ensuring the successful typed IR has not been converted into a generator state machine. Tests should distinguish nesting from an ordinary block or an await operand. No new code-generation or state-machine subsystem is required by this claim; that lowering is explicitly excluded here.

Performed source inspection with review start/read only. No source changes or behavioral tests were performed; coordinator-run suites remain separate execution evidence. No requested edits: the current implementation and test TODO retains the unimplemented representation explicitly and does not weaken the specification.
